title: Monotonicity of aborting decision time
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, $L$ a language of binary strings, and $T_1,T_2:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ time bounds. Suppose that on every input $x$, every branch of $N$ halts after $T_1(|x|)$ choices, no such branch outputs the one-bit string encoding the complement of membership in $L$, and the probability of outputting the one-bit membership value is at least $1/2$. If $T_1(n)\le T_2(n)$ for every $n$, then the same guarantees hold with time bound $T_2$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet
$L$ is a language of binary strings
$N$ satisfies the stated aborting decision conditions with time bound $T_1$
